questions.subject: Routine Vaccination
questions.title: Vaccine included in the Yemeni immunization program
questions.originalQuestion: Yemeni program of vaccines all following except:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Influenza vaccine is not part of the routine Yemeni childhood vaccination program represented by the question; diphtheria-containing vaccines, MMR, and hepatitis B are routine program vaccines.

optionExplanations.A: Diphtheria-containing vaccines are part of routine childhood immunization.
optionExplanations.B: MMR is a routine childhood vaccine.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: influenza vaccination is not listed as a routine vaccine in the program represented by this question.
optionExplanations.D: Hepatitis B vaccination is part of routine immunization.

questions.subject: Vaccine Adverse Events
questions.title: Rotavirus vaccine and intussusception
questions.originalQuestion: Which one of the following vaccines complicated by Intestinal intussusception:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Rotavirus vaccination has a rare association with intussusception, particularly shortly after vaccination.

optionExplanations.A: Hepatitis B vaccine is not the classic vaccine associated with intussusception.
optionExplanations.B: Diphtheria-containing vaccines are not the classic cause of intussusception.
optionExplanations.C: Influenza vaccine is not the classic vaccine associated with intussusception.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: rotavirus vaccine has a small increased risk of intussusception.

questions.subject: Pregnancy Vaccination
questions.title: Live vaccines avoided during pregnancy
questions.originalQuestion: What the vaccine avoided in 1st month of pregnancy:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: MMR is a live attenuated vaccine and is contraindicated during pregnancy. Inactivated influenza, tetanus-containing vaccines, and hepatitis B can be used when indicated.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: MMR is a live attenuated vaccine and should not be given during pregnancy.
optionExplanations.B: Inactivated influenza vaccination is recommended during pregnancy when indicated.
optionExplanations.C: Tetanus-containing vaccination can be given during pregnancy when indicated.
optionExplanations.D: Hepatitis B vaccination can be given when indicated during pregnancy.
optionExplanations.E: Diphtheria-containing vaccines may be administered as part of indicated tetanus-diphtheria-containing vaccination.

questions.subject: Intrinsic and Extrinsic Pathways
questions.title: Factor not assessed by the intrinsic pathway
questions.originalQuestion: PTT factors are all of the following except:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: aPTT primarily evaluates the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways. Factor VII belongs to the extrinsic pathway and is assessed by PT rather than aPTT.

optionExplanations.A: Factor VIII is part of the intrinsic pathway.
optionExplanations.B: Factor XI is part of the intrinsic pathway.
optionExplanations.C: Factor X is part of the common pathway and affects aPTT.
optionExplanations.D: Factor XII is part of the intrinsic pathway.
optionExplanations.E: Correct: factor VII belongs to the extrinsic pathway and is primarily assessed by PT.

questions.subject: Plasmodium falciparum Malaria
questions.title: Chloroquine sensitivity in falciparum malaria
questions.originalQuestion: All of the following are true according to falciparum malaria except:

originalOptions.E: Drug of choice is Artesunate Artemether

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: P. falciparum can cause anemia and jaundice and may present after a travel-related incubation period. Chloroquine resistance is widespread, so chloroquine sensitivity is not generally true; artemisinin-based therapy is used for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in many settings.

optionExplanations.A: Jaundice can occur in severe falciparum malaria.
optionExplanations.B: Hemolysis and malaria-related disease can produce anemia.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: widespread chloroquine resistance means falciparum malaria should not generally be considered chloroquine-sensitive.
optionExplanations.D: A travel-related illness appearing within weeks is compatible with malaria incubation and presentation.
optionExplanations.E: Artemisinin-based therapy is an accepted treatment approach for falciparum malaria; severe disease requires parenteral artesunate.

questions.subject: Glasgow Coma Scale
questions.title: Components of the Glasgow Coma Scale
questions.originalQuestion: GCS are all of the following except: -

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale consists of eye opening, verbal response, and motor response. Pupil size is assessed separately and is not a GCS component.

optionExplanations.A: Eye opening is one of the three GCS components.
optionExplanations.B: Motor response is one of the three GCS components.
optionExplanations.C: Verbal response is one of the three GCS components.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: pupil size is not part of the GCS.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the preceding options include GCS components.

questions.subject: Estimated Due Date
questions.title: EDD from LMP using Naegele's rule
questions.originalQuestion: LMP 30 June. What is the EDD?

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Using Naegele's rule, add 7 days to the first day of the LMP and subtract 3 months: 30 June → 7 July → 7 April of the following year.

optionExplanations.A: 23 March does not result from Naegele's rule for an LMP of 30 June.
optionExplanations.B: 7 March is three months too early.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: 30 June + 7 days − 3 months = 7 April.

questions.subject: Clinical Presentation
questions.title: Clinical features of colorectal cancer
questions.originalQuestion: All of the following are signs of Colorectal cancer except:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Anemia, abdominal pain, and change in bowel habits are recognized presentations of colorectal cancer. Hemorrhoids are common anorectal disease but are not a typical sign of colorectal cancer.

optionExplanations.A: Anemia, particularly iron-deficiency anemia, can occur with colorectal cancer.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: hemorrhoids are not a typical clinical sign of colorectal cancer.
optionExplanations.C: Abdominal pain can occur in colorectal cancer.
optionExplanations.D: A change in bowel habits is a classic warning symptom.

questions.subject: Secondary Raynaud Phenomenon
questions.title: Diseases associated with Raynaud phenomenon
questions.originalQuestion: Raynaud's Phenomenon is a feature of the following except.

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Raynaud phenomenon is classically associated with connective-tissue disease such as systemic sclerosis and can occur with vascular disorders including Buerger disease. Polycythemia vera is not a classic association.

optionExplanations.A: Systemic sclerosis is a classic cause of secondary Raynaud phenomenon.
optionExplanations.B: Buerger disease can be associated with digital ischemia and Raynaud-type symptoms.
optionExplanations.C: Raynaud phenomenon can occur in connective-tissue disease including rheumatoid arthritis.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: polycythemia vera is not a classic association with Raynaud phenomenon.

questions.subject: Life Expectancy
questions.title: Life expectancy in Yemen
questions.originalQuestion: The expected life age (years) in Yemen is:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: The source presents 66 years as the expected life expectancy figure. Exact life expectancy varies by year and data source, so this answer is tied to the examination's intended dataset rather than a universal current value.

optionExplanations.B: 44 years is substantially lower than the expected life expectancy figure.

questions.subject: Host-Agent-Environment Relationship
questions.title: Equilibrium of host, agent and environment
questions.originalQuestion: The equilibrium between host, agent C environment is termed:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: In the terminology used by this question, a stable equilibrium among host, agent, and environment is associated with endemicity. The epidemiologic triad itself describes the interaction among these three components.

optionExplanations.A: Correct in the terminology intended by the question: endemicity reflects a relatively stable disease presence in a population.
optionExplanations.B: An epidemic is an occurrence above the expected level, not simply equilibrium.
optionExplanations.C: A pandemic is an epidemic spreading across multiple countries or continents.
optionExplanations.D: An outbreak is a localized occurrence above expected levels.

questions.subject: Diagnostic Findings
questions.title: Kayser-Fleischer rings in Wilson disease
questions.originalQuestion: . One of the following is diagnostic

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Kayser-Fleischer rings are a characteristic finding of Wilson disease and, in the appropriate clinical context, strongly support the diagnosis. ANA is supportive but not specific for SLE, and RBC casts indicate glomerular bleeding rather than a single specific disease.

optionExplanations.A: Erythema nodosum is a reaction pattern and is not diagnostic of leprosy.
optionExplanations.B: ANA is sensitive for SLE but is not specific or by itself diagnostic.
optionExplanations.C: RBC casts indicate glomerular inflammation or bleeding but are not specific for one diagnosis.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: Kayser-Fleischer rings are characteristic of Wilson disease.

questions.subject: Electrolyte Disturbances
questions.title: Serum sodium changes in DKA
questions.originalQuestion: About DKA, Hyperglycemia is associated:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Hyperglycemia causes osmotic water movement from the intracellular to extracellular space, lowering measured serum sodium concentration (translocational or dilutional hyponatremia).

optionExplanations.A: Magnesium abnormalities can occur in DKA but are not the characteristic association asked here.
optionExplanations.B: Hypernatremia is not the usual measured sodium effect of marked hyperglycemia before correction for glucose.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: hyperglycemia commonly produces dilutional/translocational hyponatremia.
optionExplanations.D: Calcium abnormalities are not the principal association described by the question.

questions.subject: Seizure vs Syncope
questions.title: Feature favoring syncope rather than seizure
questions.originalQuestion: Scenario about a person who fall down suddenly - Which one of the following makes you exculde seizure

originalOptions.B: Awake suddenly C Return to normal state with feeling of weakness.

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.correction: The source option B is malformed/contains an embedded option label. The clinical concept intended appears to be rapid recovery without a postictal state.
questions.correctedQuestion: Which feature favors syncope rather than a generalized seizure after a sudden fall?

correctAnswer.text: B — Sudden recovery/return to normal state favors syncope

questions.explanation: Rapid recovery of consciousness without a prolonged postictal state favors syncope rather than generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The source option is malformed and contains an apparent embedded option label, so its wording is preserved exactly.

optionExplanations.A: A tonic-clonic event strongly supports a generalized seizure.
optionExplanations.B: Correct in intent: rapid return to normal consciousness favors syncope, although the source wording is malformed.
optionExplanations.C: Tongue laceration, especially lateral tongue biting, supports seizure.
optionExplanations.D: An aura before loss of consciousness supports seizure.

questions.subject: Source/Reservoir Control
questions.title: Measures that control the source of infection
questions.originalQuestion: Control Source of infection by all of the following except:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Control of an infection source includes treating infected patients and carriers and controlling reservoirs. Good nutrition supports host health but is not a direct source-control measure.

optionExplanations.A: Treating carriers can eliminate a source of infection.
optionExplanations.B: Reservoir control is a direct communicable-disease control measure.
optionExplanations.C: Treating infected patients can reduce infectious sources.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: good nutrition is supportive prevention, not direct source control.

questions.subject: Immediate Postpartum Complications
questions.title: Abnormal finding requiring concern after vaginal delivery
questions.originalQuestion: Uncomplicated vaginal delivery. What to worry about within1 hour?

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Marked abdominal rigidity after delivery is concerning for an acute intra-abdominal or uterine complication and warrants assessment. A heart rate of 60 can be normal, mild leukocytosis is physiologic postpartum, and isolated temperature elevation has to be interpreted in context.

optionExplanations.A: A heart rate of 60/min can be normal in a stable postpartum patient.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: abdominal rigidity is abnormal and can indicate a serious intra-abdominal or uterine problem.
optionExplanations.C: A single temperature of 38°C requires clinical context and confirmation rather than automatically indicating a complication.
optionExplanations.D: Proteinuria is not the key immediate postpartum danger represented by this question.
optionExplanations.E: Leukocytosis is common physiologically after labor and is not by itself diagnostic of infection.

questions.subject: Secondary Amenorrhea
questions.title: Most common cause of secondary amenorrhea
questions.originalQuestion: The most common cause of 2ry Amenorrhea is:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Pregnancy is the most common physiologic cause of secondary amenorrhea and should be excluded first in a reproductive-age patient.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: pregnancy is the most common cause of secondary amenorrhea.

questions.subject: Benign vs Malignant Bone Tumors
questions.title: Metastatic potential of bone tumors
questions.originalQuestion: The main difference between benign C malignant bone tumors is:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: The key biologic distinction is malignant potential, including the ability to invade and metastasize. Growth rate, pain, and location may overlap and are not by themselves definitive.

optionExplanations.A: Growth rate can differ but is not the defining distinction.
optionExplanations.B: Pain can occur in both benign and malignant bone tumors.
optionExplanations.C: Location alone cannot reliably distinguish benign from malignant tumors.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: malignant tumors have malignant invasive/metastatic potential, unlike benign tumors.

questions.subject: Early Pregnancy Loss
questions.title: Abortion as a major category of pregnancy loss
questions.originalQuestion: Most prominent Cause of Pregnancy loss is:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Among the listed choices, abortion represents a pregnancy loss occurring before viability and is the intended answer in this question.

optionExplanations.A: Stillbirth is a later pregnancy outcome and is not the intended broad category here.
optionExplanations.B: Contraceptive pills do not constitute a cause of pregnancy loss in this classification.
optionExplanations.C: Correct for the terminology and choices provided: abortion is pregnancy loss before viability.
optionExplanations.D: Neonatal death occurs after birth and is not pregnancy loss.

questions.subject: Imagery Therapy
questions.title: Classification of imagination-based therapy
questions.originalQuestion: Imagination treatment is type of

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.correction: The terminology in the source is nonstandard and does not permit a reliable single-best answer.
questions.correctedQuestion: Which type of psychological intervention uses guided imagery or therapeutic imagination?

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined reliably from the provided options

questions.explanation: The term 'imagination treatment' is not a sufficiently standardized medical term to map confidently to one of the three options. Guided imagery is a psychological/behavioral technique, but the source choices do not provide a clear standard classification.

optionExplanations.A: Herbal therapy involves medicinal plants and is not synonymous with guided imagery.
optionExplanations.B: 'Subconscious therapy' is not a standard diagnostic classification for guided imagery.

questions.subject: Acute Cholera Management
questions.title: First-line treatment of cholera
questions.originalQuestion: patient with vibreo Cholera, first line treatment

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.correction: The question asks for first-line treatment but provides only antibiotics. Rehydration is the first-line treatment.
questions.correctedQuestion: What is the first-line treatment for a patient with cholera?

correctAnswer.text: No valid single answer from the listed options; prompt should identify rehydration as first-line treatment

questions.explanation: The first-line treatment of cholera is prompt and adequate rehydration, preferably oral rehydration solution for patients who can drink and intravenous fluids for severe dehydration. Antibiotics are adjunctive in selected patients, not the primary first-line treatment.

optionExplanations.A: Ampicillin is not the primary first-line treatment of cholera.
optionExplanations.B: Ceftriaxone is not the routine first-line treatment of uncomplicated cholera.
optionExplanations.C: Azithromycin can be used as an antimicrobial option in selected cholera cases but is not the primary first-line treatment.
optionExplanations.D: Doxycycline is an effective antimicrobial option for cholera in appropriate patients, but rehydration remains first-line treatment.

questions.subject: Community Health Assessment
questions.title: Steps/components of community diagnosis
questions.originalQuestion: In Community Diagnosis in Communicable disease all true except:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Defining community problems, correlating identified problems, and developing proposals/interventions fit community diagnosis processes. 'Disaster implication' is not a standard core step as phrased.

optionExplanations.A: Defining the community problem is part of community diagnosis.
optionExplanations.B: Relating or correlating identified problems can be part of community assessment.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: disaster implication is not a standard core step of community diagnosis as phrased.
optionExplanations.D: Developing a new proposal/intervention follows assessment and prioritization.

questions.subject: Hepatic Hydatid Cyst
questions.title: Indications for surgery in hepatic hydatid cyst
questions.originalQuestion: Indications of surgery in hydatid liver cyst are all except:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Indications for intervention include complications such as infection, pressure on adjacent structures, and high risk of rupture. A completely calcified inactive cyst is generally not an indication for surgery unless other complications exist.

optionExplanations.A: An infected hydatid cyst can require intervention.
optionExplanations.B: Compression of adjacent structures is an indication for intervention.
optionExplanations.C: High risk of rupture is an indication for treatment/intervention.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: a completely calcified inactive cyst is generally not an indication for surgery by itself.

questions.subject: Pap Smear
questions.title: Indications and findings of Pap smear
questions.originalQuestion: Pap Smear indicated in all except:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Pap cytology is primarily used for cervical cancer screening and may report inflammatory/reactive changes and some organisms such as Trichomonas. It is not a diagnostic test for gonorrhea.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: gonorrhea is diagnosed using appropriate microbiologic testing, not Pap smear cytology.
optionExplanations.B: Cervical cancer/cervical precancer is the principal target of cervical cytology screening.
optionExplanations.C: Inflammatory/reactive changes may be reported on cytology.
optionExplanations.D: Trichomonas organisms may sometimes be identified incidentally on Pap cytology.

questions.subject: Lower Motor Neuron Signs
questions.title: Clinical signs of lower motor neuron lesions
questions.originalQuestion: which of the following are signs C symptoms of LMN:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Lower motor neuron lesions classically produce weakness, reduced tone, reduced reflexes, muscle wasting, and fasciculations. Flaccid hypotonia is therefore characteristic.

optionExplanations.A: An extensor plantar response is an upper motor neuron sign.
optionExplanations.B: Clonus is an upper motor neuron sign.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: LMN lesions produce flaccid weakness and hypotonia.
optionExplanations.D: A positive Babinski sign is an upper motor neuron sign.
optionExplanations.E: Hypertonia is associated with upper motor neuron lesions.

questions.subject: Pneumonia Complications
questions.title: Complications of pneumonia
questions.originalQuestion: Complications of Pneumonia include all of the following except:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Pneumonia can be complicated by parapneumonic effusion, empyema, pneumothorax, and sepsis. Endocarditis is not a typical direct complication of pneumonia.

optionExplanations.A: Pleural effusion is a recognized complication of pneumonia.
optionExplanations.B: Empyema is a recognized complication of bacterial pneumonia.
optionExplanations.C: Pneumothorax can occur as a complication, particularly with severe infection or necrosis.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: endocarditis is not a typical direct complication of pneumonia.
optionExplanations.E: Sepsis is a serious systemic complication of pneumonia.

questions.subject: Serious Illness in Infants
questions.title: Differential diagnosis of a very ill infant
questions.originalQuestion: Baby presented with Poor feeding lethargy and he is very ill. What could it be?

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Poor feeding and lethargy in a very ill infant are nonspecific but potentially serious signs. Sepsis, meningitis, and inborn errors of metabolism are all important possibilities requiring urgent assessment.

optionExplanations.A: Sepsis can present with poor feeding, lethargy, and severe illness in infants.
optionExplanations.B: Meningitis can present with nonspecific systemic signs in young infants.
optionExplanations.C: Inborn errors of metabolism can present with poor feeding, lethargy, and acute decompensation.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: all three are important differential diagnoses.

questions.subject: Pulmonary Tuberculosis Diagnosis
questions.title: Definitive diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis
questions.originalQuestion: The definitive diagnosis of Pulmonary TB:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Microbiological demonstration of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, using appropriate bacteriological or molecular testing, provides definitive confirmation. Clinical and radiologic findings support but do not by themselves confirm active pulmonary TB.

optionExplanations.A: Clinical diagnosis can be presumptive but is not definitive confirmation.
optionExplanations.B: Radiology supports the diagnosis but cannot definitively identify M. tuberculosis.
optionExplanations.C: Serology is not the standard definitive diagnostic method for pulmonary TB.
optionExplanations.D: Immunologic tests such as TST/IGRA indicate infection but do not establish active pulmonary TB.

questions.subject: Causes of Ascites
questions.title: Differential diagnosis of ascites
questions.originalQuestion: All of the following are causes of ascitis except:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.correction: The question is poorly constructed because more than one listed condition can cause ascites.
questions.correctedQuestion: Which of the following is NOT a recognized cause of ascites? Provide options with only one clearly incorrect cause.

correctAnswer.text: No valid single answer can be established confidently from the listed options

questions.explanation: Several listed conditions can be associated with ascites. Budd-Chiari syndrome, pancreatitis, severe hypothyroidism/myxedema, and malignancy can all produce ascites; severe liver disease can also be associated with fluid accumulation. The wording does not provide a reliable single exception.

optionExplanations.A: Budd-Chiari syndrome can cause portal hypertension and ascites.
optionExplanations.B: Pancreatic disease can cause pancreatic ascites.
optionExplanations.C: Severe hypothyroidism/myxedema can rarely cause ascites.
optionExplanations.D: Gastric malignancy can cause malignant ascites, especially with peritoneal spread.
optionExplanations.E: Severe liver disease can be associated with ascites; the exact context is insufficient to make this the unique exception.

questions.subject: Clinical Features and Epidemiology
questions.title: Clinical and epidemiologic features of COVID-19
questions.originalQuestion: Covid-19 all of the following are true except:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

correctAnswer.text: B — Most common manifestation is Pneumonia

questions.explanation: Most SARS-CoV-2 infections are asymptomatic or mild, commonly presenting with upper-respiratory or nonspecific symptoms. Pneumonia is an important manifestation, especially in severe disease, but is not the most common manifestation overall.

optionExplanations.A: Risk of severe COVID-19 increases with older age, while severe disease can also occur in other age groups.
optionExplanations.B: Correct as the exception: pneumonia is not the most common manifestation across all infections; many cases are asymptomatic or mild.
optionExplanations.C: An incubation period around 2–14 days was classically used in early COVID-19 descriptions.
optionExplanations.D: The stated mortality figure reflects an early-pandemic estimate and varies substantially by population, variant, vaccination, and treatment.

questions.subject: RBC Maturation
questions.title: Changes during red blood cell maturation
questions.originalQuestion: All are true about maturation of RBCs except:

originalOptions.A: Reduction in size of normoblast.with mature
originalOptions.B: Change in color of normoblast with mature
originalOptions.C: DNA synthesis increase in maturation RBCs

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

correctAnswer.text: C — DNA synthesis increase in maturation RBCs

questions.explanation: During erythroid maturation, cells become smaller, hemoglobinization changes their color, and the nucleus is ultimately extruded. DNA synthesis decreases and stops as cells mature, so an increase is false.

optionExplanations.A: Erythroid cells generally decrease in size during maturation.
optionExplanations.B: Cell color changes as hemoglobin accumulates during maturation.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: DNA synthesis does not increase; it progressively decreases and stops before mature RBC formation.
optionExplanations.D: The nucleus is extruded during terminal erythroid maturation.

questions.subject: Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms
questions.title: Symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia
questions.originalQuestion: The symptoms in benign prostatic hypertrophy all following are true except:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: BPH commonly causes obstructive and irritative lower urinary tract symptoms such as hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia, and urgency. Gross hematuria is not a classic symptom and should prompt evaluation for another cause, although bleeding can occur in BPH.

optionExplanations.A: Hesitancy is a common obstructive LUTS in BPH.
optionExplanations.B: Nocturia/frequency is common in BPH.
optionExplanations.C: Weak urinary stream is a common obstructive symptom.
optionExplanations.D: Urgency can occur as an irritative LUTS.
optionExplanations.E: Correct for the classic symptom profile: gross hematuria is not a typical defining symptom and requires evaluation.

questions.subject: Quadriceps Contracture
questions.title: Common cause of quadriceps contracture
questions.originalQuestion: The most common cause of quadriceps contracture is:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Quadriceps contracture is classically associated with fibrosis after repeated intramuscular injections into the thigh, particularly in children in settings where this practice has occurred.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: post-injection fibrosis is a classic cause of quadriceps contracture.
optionExplanations.B: Femoral shaft fracture can lead to stiffness but is not the classic common cause in this question.
optionExplanations.C: Ischemic muscle injury can cause contracture but is not the intended common cause.
optionExplanations.D: Congenital contracture is not the typical cause.
optionExplanations.E: Operations may cause scarring but are not the classic common cause.

questions.subject: Intramedullary Nailing
questions.title: Contraindication to intramedullary nailing
questions.originalQuestion: One of the following is contraindication of intramedulary nail use..:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.explanation: Traditional teaching considers intramedullary nailing relatively contraindicated in skeletally immature children depending on the bone, nail type, and growth plate. Modern pediatric techniques use age- and fracture-specific flexible or other nails, so the source statement is context-dependent.

optionExplanations.A: A fracture at a narrowest part can still be treated with appropriate fixation depending on location and anatomy.
optionExplanations.B: Correct according to the traditional teaching represented by the question: standard rigid intramedullary nailing is generally avoided in skeletally immature children when it risks the physis.
optionExplanations.C: Transverse fractures can be treated with intramedullary nails in appropriate bones.
optionExplanations.D: Nonunion is an accepted indication for revision fixation, including intramedullary nailing in suitable cases.
optionExplanations.E: Open/compound fractures are not an absolute contraindication; management depends on contamination, soft tissue status, and fracture characteristics.

questions.subject: Perioperative DKA Management
questions.title: Insulin infusion during perioperative pediatric DKA
questions.originalQuestion: A child with known case of DKA and Acute appendicitis prepared for surgery, Insulin given prior operation. At the OT glucose level raised to 180mg/dL, What should be given:

sourceAnswer.text: Not provided in the source file.

questions.correction: The question omits the units, weight basis, and dosing interval required to safely select an insulin infusion rate.
questions.correctedQuestion: In a child with DKA undergoing surgery, with blood glucose 180 mg/dL, what weight-based insulin infusion rate should be used, and should dextrose-containing fluid be added?

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined reliably from the source because the insulin units, weight basis, and intended dosing interval are missing

questions.explanation: Initial management of uncomplicated anterior epistaxis is firm, continuous compression of the soft part of the nose while the patient leans forward. Packing or specialist intervention is considered if bleeding persists or is severe.
